title: docs site: frontmatter carries no short sidebar label — one title serves SERP, h1, nav and llms.txt
body:
## One-liner

A doc page's frontmatter `title` is simultaneously the SERP `<title>`, the on-page `h1`, the sidebar/nav label and the `llms.txt` entry — consumers with different length budgets, all served by one string. There is no separate short label for navigation.

> ⚠️ **Body repaired 2026-09-01.** The original text was lost to a sanitizer truncation on write — it ended mid-sentence at ``the SERP ` ``, flagged by triage in `issuecomment-5414435717` and unrepaired for seven days while #12237 sat blocked on this card. The text below is a **re-measurement from `origin/main`, not a recovery of the original**; angle-bracketed tokens are in backticks so the write survives. The filer (@os-zhuang) or the #12243 epic PM should correct anything the original carried that this misses.

## Measured — `origin/main` @ `479ace6`, 2026-09-01

Every page carries exactly two frontmatter keys, and neither is a nav label:

```
frontmatter keys across content/docs/**/*.mdx     n = 405 pages
  title:        405
  description:  405
  (no other key appears on any page)
```

Title length on the same tree:

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| pages | 405 |
| median title length | 14 |
| titles <= 20 chars | 327 |
| titles carrying ` — ` | 7 |
| titles in the 50–60 band | **0** |
| longest title | 42 |

## The consumers of `page.data.title`

`apps/docs/source.config.ts` uses the stock `pageSchema` from `fumadocs-core/source/schema`, so `title` is the only string any of these can read:

| consumer | site |
|---|---|
| SERP `<title>` | `apps/docs/app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx:211` (`generateMetadata`) |
| on-page `h1` | `page.tsx:150` — `<DocsTitle>{page.data.title}</DocsTitle>` |
| sidebar / nav tree | `apps/docs/lib/source.ts:6` — `loader()` builds the page tree from the same `title` |
| `llms.txt` | `apps/docs/app/llms.txt/route.ts:10` |
| OG card image | `apps/docs/app/og/docs/[...slug]/route.tsx:18` |
| JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` + `headline`/`name` | `page.tsx:95`, `:123`, `:124` |

⇒ The card's title says four; the measurement says **six**. The two extra — the OG card and the JSON-LD — are the ones a title-lengthening PR would reshape without anyone noticing.

## Why this blocks #12237

#12237 wants 50–60 character titles carrying search intent. **4 of its 180 rows have landed** (PR #12312, commit `e18c870b`), and the commit message names the reason it stopped there: *"four **sidebar-free** page titles"*. A page with no sidebar entry can take a long title immediately; the remaining 176 cannot, because the same string is the nav label — lengthening them makes the sidebar unreadable.

⇒ This card is the **enabling half**: give the frontmatter a short nav label and #12237's 176-row table applies on top. #12237 records that dependency as `Blocked-by: #12311`.

## What the work is

Three sub-questions, none pre-judged here:

1. **Where the short label lives** — a new frontmatter key (`navTitle` / `sidebarTitle`), or a per-page override in the 35 existing `content/docs/**/meta.json` files. Both are real; the meta.json route needs no schema change but splits the label away from the page it names.
2. **How it is wired** — `source.config.ts` already demonstrates the extension pattern in this repo (`blogSchema = pageSchema.extend({ … })`), so a schema extension plus a page-tree transform in `apps/docs/lib/source.ts` is the shape. `fumadocs-core` is pinned at `16.14.4`; check whether it offers a first-class hook before adding a custom transform.
3. **What happens when the key is absent** — the fallback must be `title`, so all 405 pages keep working on day one and a label is added only where a title has been lengthened.

## Acceptance

- [ ] a doc page can declare a nav label distinct from its `title`, with `title` as the documented fallback
- [ ] the sidebar renders the short label; SERP `<title>`, `h1`, `llms.txt` and the OG card keep reading `title`
- [ ] the mechanism is written down somewhere #12237's 176-row rewrite can cite
- [ ] `pnpm check:doc-anchors` and the link checker stay green

## Parent / downstream

Parent: **#12243** (epic — docs-site indexability, p0). Downstream: **#12237** (`pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #12311`, p1 — 176 rows waiting on this).
